solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cop on trail of ecstasy drew blank

indicators.note: a cop following behind ecstasy is written after it

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
MP, military police, are cops
teams that drew a match tied it

explanation.surface: A police officer chasing a drug dealer comes away with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drew blank' reads as one idiom, but 'drew' gives TIED and 'blank' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has had all its contents removed is left blank, vacant.

clue.text: Thus see a moderate …

parts.note: the letters of the word for comfort, sent off (mixed up), give the words see a: the answer itself is the instruction

explanation.surface: A cryptic opener that runs on into the next clue, as if introducing a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, an anagram of EASE with OFF as its signal, and it yields SEE A, which is what the clue prints; 'Thus' points at that.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to slacken or lessen in intensity, a sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: … diplomat not wanted as Republican in Pentagon, NASA or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unwelcome envoy is barred from American defence and space bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into PENTAGON NASA OR and the whole lot is rearranged by 'otherwise'; 'as' and 'in' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names an envoy a host country has declared unacceptable, so not wanted.

clue.text: Agent virtually upended into plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, upended means the word is turned bottom to top, reading backwards

parts.note: Siri is Apple's virtual assistant, an agent existing only virtually

explanation.surface: A spy is somehow turned upside down into a planted position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent virtually' is not 'almost an agent' but a virtual agent, Apple's voice assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag and its relatives are a genus of flowering garden perennials.

clue.text: Twin powers in charge here, properly including work with oxygen

indicators.note: properly's synonym takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: duly means properly, in the right way
OP, short for opus, is a work
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Two rulers govern correctly, working with an oxygen supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A market or realm controlled by two dominant parties is where twin powers are in charge.

clue.text: Winger's row with The Bhoys' left half

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the left half of a word is its first half

parts.note: The Bhoys is the nickname of Celtic, the Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A footballer's wing play is debated, along with Celtic's left-half position.
explanation.walkthrough: Winger and left half look like football positions; the winger is a bird, and left half is the opening half of CELTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiercel is a male hawk or falcon, a creature that flies on wings.

clue.text: Nick's typist possibly sitting on terrace

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker, perhaps a typist
Ter. is a standard address abbreviation for Terrace

explanation.surface: Someone's typist, perhaps, is sitting out on the terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is the Devil, the great tempter of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil, nicknamed Old Nick, is the archetypal seducer luring people into sin.

clue.text: Direction of Evita somewhat peripheral throughout

indicators.note: take the outside letters of every word in turn, the periphery of each

explanation.surface: A query about how the musical Evita treats its somewhat marginal material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is fodder: the ends of Evita and somewhat give EA and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal compass points is a direction.

clue.text: With backbone mostly fixed, queen's in good health for game

parts.note: a chine is the backbone of an animal

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: set means fixed

indicators.note: the queen is placed inside the toast

parts.note: cheers and good health are both drinking toasts
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: After spinal surgery, the Queen is healthy enough to play.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a board game of marbles hopping across a six-pointed star board.

clue.text: Sheds unproductive tools regularly …

parts.note: lean years are unproductive ones

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone sheds their useless tools from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like a verb; it is the noun plural, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple sloping-roofed shelters built against a wall are sheds.

clue.text: It's a sound manoeuvre if in storm at sea, stowing sails at the earliest

indicators.note: only the earliest letter of sails is used
to manoeuvre the letters is to move them about into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to sailors to reef their sails when caught in a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sound' is a sea channel, not a noise; this one separates Sicily from mainland Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow sea channel, and this is the channel between Sicily and Italy.

clue.text: Malodour within old English instrument

indicators.note: the body odour goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a malodour

explanation.surface: A bad smell inside an antique English musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: At heart Eleanor thinks: 'Significant point'

indicators.note: the answer sits in the heart of the words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Eleanor is privately convinced she has made a significant point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal compass point is a significant point of the compass.

clue.text: Lift the man by feet

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man is lifted up by his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something to gauge its weight is to lift it.

clue.text: … to maintain shell protecting core of machinery

indicators.note: the shell is wrapped around the other piece, protecting it

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish, here standing for a shell

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the shed clue: tools, then a casing that protects a machine's core.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or insist something is true is to maintain it.

clue.text: Lyric — working theatre?

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Is the Lyric a working theatre?
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric looks like a London theatre's name, but it is the poem. The question mark flags a cinema as an example of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema chain's houses are picture theatres, so it is an example.

clue.text: Trial arranged within following year is failing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the two abbreviations
arranged means put into a new order

explanation.surface: A court trial set for the coming year is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' looks like a verb but is a noun here, a weakness of character.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakness or moral flaw is a failing, a noun here.

clue.text: Don once again put right

definitions.meaning: to don is to put on clothes, so to don once again is to clothe again
to remedy or rectify a wrong

explanation.surface: Getting dressed again to set something right.
explanation.definitionFit: To rectify a grievance is to put it right; and with a hyphen, to clothe again.

clue.text: Greatly enjoying song and dance band

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, an ado
a ring is a band, as worn on the finger

explanation.surface: Someone loves a musical act that both sings and dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' is the idiom for a fuss, not a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping or loving something very much is greatly enjoying it.

clue.text: Supportive plays Neddy put on Irish stage totally slated initially

parts.note: Neddy is a pet name for a donkey, an ass
I is the abbreviation for Irish

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Plays with a donkey on the Irish stage were totally panned at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like drama, but it is football or hockey moves that help a scorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes leading directly to a goal are counted as supporting plays in sport.

clue.text: Machinist joining this business involved in organic chemistry

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic joins a firm working in organic chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of Machinist joined with the answer's rearrange to give ORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling food and household goods is a grocer's business, here organic produce.

clue.text: Plonker! That chap'd get carpeted!

parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool, a clot
that chap'd contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: An idiot who would surely be reprimanded by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get carpeted' is British slang for a telling-off, but here carpeted is covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor that is carpeted is covered, dressed in fabric.

clue.text: Steel left after split with Jenny

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left comes after the word for split

parts.note: to split is to cut
a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

explanation.surface: Steel abandoned after a break-up with a woman called Jenny.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a woman's name; it is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is a poetic word for a sword, and this is a short curved sword.

clue.text: Wants losses to cover end of year

indicators.note: the deaths enclose the letter, covering it

parts.note: deaths are losses of life

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A firm's deficits are needed to offset the year-end figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortages or scarcities are wants, as in lack.

clue.text: Maybe Beowulf's a delight, upon reflection?

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a gas is a delight, something great fun

explanation.surface: A reader muses whether the Old English poem Beowulf is a pleasure to read.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old English poem is a long heroic tale, an example of the epic form.

clue.text: This player — EastEnders' Outhwaite — is captivating

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A charming actress named Outhwaite from the BBC soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London. Player means a seat at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, so this is one player.

clue.text: Water colour

definitions.meaning: Latin for water, used in pharmacy and chemistry

explanation.surface: A watercolour painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for water also names a pale blue-green colour.

clue.text: Samuel's heading into the rain — to find Timothy, say?

indicators.note: the initial letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the rain is the wet, as in come in out of the wet

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter

explanation.surface: Samuel heads out into the rain to find his father Timothy.
explanation.walkthrough: Timothy West is a British actor, and Samuel West, also an actor, is his son.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Timothy carries this surname, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Daffy coming from the deep to bowl over

indicators.note: rising up from the depths, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: daffy and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Daffy Duck surfaces from the deep to knock someone flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or amaze someone is to bowl them over.

clue.text: US diplomatic agency attempts a tender illegitimately

indicators.note: improperly arrived at, so the letters are in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put in a bid by underhand means.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the federal department that runs American foreign affairs and diplomacy.

clue.text: Growth in effort to become well-tanned?

indicators.note: the growth sits inside the effort

parts.note: a shy is a try or attempt, as at a coconut shy
a wart is a growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Is a skin growth caused by trying to get a deep tan?
explanation.definitionFit: Dark-skinned or dusky in complexion, as someone well bronzed may look.

clue.text: Chambers errs about 'utility'

indicators.note: the word for sins goes around the other piece

parts.note: to err is to sin
utility is use, usefulness

explanation.surface: The Chambers dictionary makes mistakes about the word utility.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers looks like the dictionary; it means hollow cavities in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-filled cavities in the bones of the face are chambers.
